paper_metadata.title: Characterization of Fe3Al-based intermetallic alloys fabricated by mechanical alloying and HIP consolidation

evidence.quote: Fe3Al-based alloys with and without Ti addition were synthesized by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) of mechanically alloyed nanocrystalline powders.

One is the ordering strengthening effect, because the Ti addition increases the degree of ordering of the compacted Fe3Al alloy.
The other is the dispersion strengthening effect. Ti addition also leads to the formation of some fine disposoids, which can act as obstacles for dislocation movement during deformation.

The high strain rate sensitivity close to 0.3 and lower activation energy than creep activation energy also suggest that grain boundary sliding plays an important role in the deformation of the 10Ti alloy at temperatures above 1073 K.
As a result, the 10Ti alloy shows better deformability and visible reduction in flow stress at temperatures above 1073 K in comparison with the 0Ti alloy.

The inhibited grain growth in the 10Ti alloy is considered to be due to the presence of fine disposoids. The grain boundary pinning mechanism proposed by Zener and Smith [19] should be responsible for this behavior.
